title: User profiles: Postgres vs DynamoDB
brief: A profile service serves 8k requests/s, 90% reads. Side A stores profiles in Postgres with 5 read replicas; side B in DynamoDB on demand. Run the scenarios and decide which fits, and what would make you switch.

scenarios.label: One profile goes viral
scenarios.about: From 10 s to 30 s, 90% of requests hit one profile. DynamoDB keeps each key on one partition, and a partition has a limit.
scenarios.watch: From 10 s to 30 s one key gets 90% of requests. Watch DynamoDB turn red and the errors number climb: one partition takes it all. Postgres doesn't care which key.

scenarios.label: Writes grow to 40%
scenarios.about: At 10 s a new feature makes 40% of requests writes. Postgres has one primary for every write.
scenarios.watch: At 10 s writes grow to 40%. Watch the Postgres block's ρ go past 1: every write lands on its one primary. DynamoDB spreads writes over partitions.

scenarios.label: Steady 8k rps
scenarios.about: Both handle it. Compare the cost: servers by the hour against pay per request.
scenarios.watch: Nothing breaks, so both canvases look the same. Read the cost row in the table.

questions: Why does Postgres shrug off the viral profile while DynamoDB throttles it? How would you fix the hot key?
What limits Postgres when writes grow, and what are your options (bigger primary, sharding, another database)?
At this load, which is cheaper? What happens to that answer at 10x the traffic?
The sim doesn't model joins or cross-table queries. How would those change the choice?
hints: Look at which block throttles in each scenario, and why. Is the limit total load or load on one key?
DynamoDB allows about 6,000 eventually consistent reads/s per partition. 90% of 7.2k reads is 6.5k on one key. Postgres has a single primary capped near 3k queries/s, and it takes every write.

DynamoDB: a cache (DAX or Redis) in front of hot keys, or spread the key. Postgres: writes need a bigger primary or sharding, and read replicas don't help. Postgres is cheaper at a steady 8k/s; DynamoDB costs scale with requests but need no capacity planning.
_notes: Graph: client -> lb -> api (20 x 1k) -> profiles. Postgres: primary + 5 read replicas, 3k/node (estimate): primary gets 800 writes + 7.2k/6 reads = 2k (rho 0.67); $0.225 x 6. DynamoDB on demand: 40k table cap, 6k reads / 1k writes per partition; $0.0625/M eventual reads, $0.625/M writes. Sim at 8k: p99 32 ms on both, cost $3.38 vs $5.45/hr. Hot key 0.9 (10-30 s): hot reads 6.48k > 6k, so DynamoDB throttles ~480/s (1.4% over the run); Postgres unaffected. Writes 40%: Postgres primary 3.2k writes + 0.8k reads = 4k > 3k: errors 8.8%, p99 2.6 s; DynamoDB fine but $9.19/hr. Not modeled: joins, transactions, item size. Checked in frontend/src/lessons/content.test.ts.
